structure does NOT beat sequence on identical proteins with an identical split. The fold geometry a monomer carries adds nothing here that the sequence does not already carry, and the dark-gene inference should be run from sequence at 1.3 s per protein rather than from ~9,600 structure downloads. This does not say 3D is useless in general -- it says the monomer-geometry version of it is not what is missing.
Y5 esm35+structure minus esm35: -0.0012 sem 0.0009 = -1.3 sem
structure does not add to sequence either. Both gates point the same way and the 3D pipeline is not justified on this evidence.
k-NN is a floor on what a representation supports, not a ceiling; a trained model can
extract more than a nearest-neighbour vote from the same vectors.
Labels come from Human-GEM's own gene-protein-reaction rules, so a wrong or missing
association is scored as if the model were right.
AlphaFold monomers carry no ligand, no cofactor and no partner, so any function that
lives in a complex is invisible to BOTH arms -- this is not a test of structure in
general, it is a test of monomer geometry.
The dark genes are dark partly because they are unlike these 2,178, so every number
here is an upper bound on what the same method would do on them.
